messages.content: What goes wrong when farmers do not stock my broiler house?

Overcrowding is the most common avoidable mistake in a small broiler house. Too many birds in the space raises litter moisture, which raises ammonia, which damages the birds' airways and opens the door to disease. Growth slows and mortality rises even when feed is good. If the litter is wet and the house smells sharp when you walk in, you are overstocked or under-ventilated.
I farm in the derived zone. What should I be growing?

Transition zone, in places two peaks of rain, supporting an early and a late crop. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake.
Any advice on how to know when grain is dry enough to store?

Grain must be dry enough before storage, around thirteen percent moisture, or it will heat, mould and be eaten by insects whatever else you do. Grain that feels dry in the afternoon sun is often still too wet, because the surface dries faster than the inside. Bite tests and the sound of grain poured into a tin are rough guides; a moisture meter at a co-operative is better.
What is the market price of maize in Kano this week?

I do not know, and I will not guess at it. Prices move week to week and by market, and a number invented by me could cost you real money at the point of sale.

For a current price, ask traders at the market itself, other farmers who sold recently, or a local farmers' association, which often tracks it.

What I can say generally is that prices are at their lowest right at harvest when everyone sells at once. If you can dry properly and store well, or sell through a cooperative that aggregates, that is usually where the gain is.
My tomato plants wilt suddenly but the leaves stay green. What should I do?

Wilting while the leaves stay green is the signature of bacterial wilt. Confirm it before spending anything.

Cut a wilting stem near the base and suspend the cut end in clear water. If a milky ooze streams out, that is bacterial wilt.

There is no chemical cure. Remove affected plants with the surrounding soil, improve drainage, and rotate away from tomato, pepper and garden egg for several seasons. A fungicide will not help.
Is there any way to deal with armyworm without buying chemicals?

Yes, and on a small plot it is often the better economics.

1. Handpick larvae out of the whorls. Done thoroughly over several days on a small field this genuinely works.
2. Destroy badly damaged plants that will not recover rather than nursing them along.
3. Intercrop so the stand is not a uniform block of maize.
4. Leave the natural enemies alone. Broad sprays kill the wasps and predators that were suppressing the pest for free.
5. After harvest, destroy crop residues, because the pest overwinters in them.

The residue step is the one most farmers skip and it is the one that reduces pressure next season.
Any advice on how to package produce for market?

Packaging is not decoration. Grading produce into uniform sizes and packing it cleanly gets a better price for exactly the same crop, because buyers pay for predictability and reject lots they must sort themselves. It also reduces damage in transit, so more of what you grew arrives saleable.
My maize stems have small holes with dry powder at the opening and the central shoot has died. What is it?

That is stem borer, not armyworm. The difference is where the damage sits.

A borer tunnels into the stem, so you see small entry holes with dry frass at the opening, and in young plants the central shoot dies while the outer leaves stay green. Split a stem lengthwise and you find the tunnel.

Armyworm feeds in the whorl at the top and leaves moist frass there instead. A spray can reach a whorl; it cannot reach a larva already inside a stem, so control here is residue destruction after harvest and early uniform planting.

The harmattan brings dry dusty air that speeds drying, which helps a harvested crop and hurts a standing one. Plan drying and storage around it and protect late vegetables from the desiccating wind.

What is the best approach to striga?

Rotation with legumes, restoring soil fertility and organic matter, hand pulling before the weed flowers and seeds, and resistant varieties where available. Small purple or pink flowered weed emerging near cereal stems, with the crop stunted and yellowed out of proportion to the visible weed. A striga problem is a soil fertility problem. It thrives where nitrogen and organic matter are depleted.
When exactly should I do this?

Rotation with legumes, restoring soil fertility and organic matter, hand pulling before the weed flowers and seeds, and resistant varieties where available. Small purple or pink flowered weed emerging near cereal stems, with the crop stunted and yellowed out of proportion to the visible weed. Give it about two weeks and compare a treated strip against an untreated one, or you cannot separate the weather from the treatment.
When should I plant oil palm?

Field plant at the start of the rains, April to June, after 10 to 12 months in the nursery. Planting at the end of the rains wastes a year of growth. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Harvest on ripeness judged by loose fruit on the ground, not by a fixed calendar. Underripe bunches give less oil, overripe raises free fatty acid and lowers quality. Fruit does not store. Free fatty acid begins rising the moment the bunch is cut, so process within 24 to 48 hours.

Check this against what your neighbours are seeing before you act on a whole field.
Can I mix two pesticides together to save time?

Do not do that on my say-so. Some combinations are unsafe or destroy each other's effect, and this varies by product.

Check both labels for what they say about tank mixing, and ask your extension officer before combining anything.

What is the right way to keep egg shell quality good?

Laying birds pull calcium out of their own bones to make shells, so a layer ration must supply enough or shells go thin and break. Shell quality falling across the whole flock at once points at the ration or at flock age, not at bad luck. Older hens lay larger eggs with the same calcium spread thinner, so shells naturally weaken late in lay. Do the cheapest thing on this list first and give it two weeks before spending more.

How do I protect a sloping field from erosion?

On sloping land, ridge along the contour rather than up and down. Ridges running downhill become channels that concentrate water, and a channel becomes a gully within a season or two. Once a gully forms it takes far more work to repair than the ridging would have cost. Keeping the surface covered, with mulch or a cover crop, protects it from rain impact.
How do I tell striga from fall armyworm on maize?

They look nothing alike once you know where to look.

Striga is a plant. You see a small purple or pink flowered weed growing at the base of the maize, and the maize is yellow and stunted out of proportion to the weed.

Fall armyworm is a caterpillar. You see ragged holes in the young leaves and moist frass packed into the whorl at the centre of the plant.

If the damage is a weed at the base, it is striga. If it is chewing damage in the funnel, it is armyworm.
There is a small purple flowering weed in my maize and the maize is yellow and stunted. I pull the weed but it keeps coming.

That is striga, and the reason pulling it has not solved the problem is that the weed is a symptom rather than the cause.

Striga attaches to the roots of the cereal and takes from the plant, which is why the maize is yellow and stunted out of all proportion to how much weed you can see. It thrives specifically where soil nitrogen and organic matter are depleted. A striga problem is a soil fertility problem wearing a disguise.

So treat it on two levels:

1. Keep pulling, but do it before the weed flowers. Each plant sheds very many long lived seeds, so allowing one season to go to seed undoes years of work.
2. Rebuild the soil. Rotate with a legume such as cowpea or soybean, return organic matter, and use nitrogen where you can afford it. Striga pressure falls as fertility recovers.

A resistant variety helps if one is available locally, but on its own it will not fix depleted ground.
I have fall armyworm but my maize is already tasselling. Should I spray?

Probably not. Fall armyworm costs you yield mainly in early vegetative growth, when the plant is small and the whorl is the growing point. On a tasselled crop the damage it can still do rarely repays the price of the spray.

What is worth doing at this stage:

1. Leave it and protect your cash.
2. Plan the residue clean-up now. Destroy the stalks after harvest instead of leaving them standing, because that is what carries the pest into next season.
3. Scout early next season, in the first weeks, rather than waiting for visible damage.

If the infestation is severe and the crop is still filling, ask your extension officer to look at it before you decide.

Just tell me how many millilitres of insecticide per litre of water for armyworm.

I will not give you a number, and I want to be clear about why rather than seem unhelpful.

The correct rate depends on the specific product in your hand. Two bottles on the same shelf can differ several times over in concentration. A number from me could mean you underdose and waste the spray, or overdose and harm yourself, the crop and whoever eats it.

The rate is printed on the label of the product you bought. Use that. If the label is missing or you cannot read it, your extension officer or the agro-dealer who sold it can tell you.

What I can tell you is where to put it: direct the spray down into the whorl where the larvae actually sit. A spray passed over the top of the leaves mostly misses them, whatever the rate.

My chickens are dying suddenly. Many died in two days. Some have twisted necks.

Sudden high mortality with twisted necks and nervous signs points strongly to Newcastle disease. Act today, because it moves fast through a flock.

What to do now:

1. Separate the birds still looking healthy from the sick ones immediately, and handle the healthy group first each time you go in.
2. Stop all movement of birds in or out. Do not sell or give away birds from this flock, and do not bring replacements in yet.
3. Dispose of dead birds by burying or burning them. Do not leave carcasses where other birds or animals reach them.
4. Contact your veterinary or extension officer today so the outbreak is known about locally.

There is no treatment that cures Newcastle once a flock breaks with it. Vaccination is the only real control, and it has to be in place before an outbreak, on schedule. Once you have restocked, keep the vaccination programme up, quarantine every new or returning bird before mixing, and never bring unsold birds back from the market straight into the flock.
What goes wrong when farmers do not decide about dry season production?

Dry season vegetable production under irrigation usually earns more than the same crop in the wet season, because supply is short and prices are higher, and disease pressure is lower. The constraint is water access and the labour of moving it. Shallow wells, washbores and simple furrow systems are within reach of many smallholders, and drip pays back fastest on high value crops.
How do I cure cassava mosaic in plants that already have it?

You cannot. It is a virus, and no spray, drench or fertiliser reverses it in an infected plant. Anyone selling you one is taking your money.

Rogue out the worst plants, accept this season's crop, and fix it at the source: take cuttings only from healthy vigorous plants next season, and use a resistant variety if one is available near you.

My groundnut is showing damage and I suspect groundnut rosette. How do I be sure?

What to look for:
- Stunted bushy plants with small distorted yellowed leaves, often in patches within the field.

Carried by aphids, worst in late planted and sparse stands. Plant early and at a dense even spacing so the canopy closes quickly, and use resistant varieties where available. Ask the older farmers in your area what has worked there, since local experience beats a general rule.
When is the best time to sell my maize?

Prices are lowest right at harvest, when everyone sells at once, so selling at the farm gate on harvest day is usually the most expensive habit in smallholder farming.

If you can dry properly and store well so quality holds, or sell through a co-operative that aggregates enough volume to reach larger buyers, that is normally where the gain is.

Can you explain cocoa farming for a beginner?

Cocoa is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems. Harvest ripe pods regularly rather than in occasional large sweeps. Frequent harvest removes disease sources and reduces losses. Fermentation and drying decide the price you are paid. Under-fermented or smoke-tainted beans are downgraded no matter how good the tree was.
I want to keep backyard chickens profitably. What should I know?

Backyard flocks give the best return on very small capital, because the birds scavenge much of their own feed. The catch is that unvaccinated local flocks are periodically wiped out by Newcastle disease, which erases years of slow gains in a fortnight. Keeping vaccination up, and supplementing scavenging with a little grain, turns a fragile flock into a reliable one. Do the cheapest thing on this list first and give it two weeks before spending more.
My tomato plants are wilting but the leaves are still green. What should I spray?

Before you buy anything, do a simple test, because if this is what I suspect then no spray will help and you would be spending money for nothing.

Cut a wilting stem near the base and suspend the cut end in a clear glass of water. Watch for a minute or two. If a milky white thread streams down from the cut into the water, that is bacterial wilt.

Wilting while the leaves stay green is the classic sign. There is no chemical cure for it. What you can do:

1. Remove affected plants along with the soil around the roots, and do not compost them.
2. Rotate away from tomato, pepper and other related crops on that ground for several seasons.
3. Improve drainage, because the bacterium moves in wet soil.

If the milky ooze does not appear, then look at root damage, nematodes or simple water stress instead, and tell me what you find.
What variety of maize is best for my farm?

I cannot answer that well without knowing more, and guessing would cost you money.

Which zone are you in, and do you want a short duration variety that escapes a short rainy season, or a longer one for higher yield? Can you buy fresh hybrid seed each season, or do you need to save seed?

Your extension officer or a nearby seed dealer will know which released varieties actually perform in your area, which is more useful than a general recommendation.
How do I tell fall armyworm apart from stem borer?

They damage different parts of the plant, and that is the reliable way to separate them.

**Fall armyworm** feeds down inside the whorl, the funnel at the growing point. You see ragged holes across the young leaves as they unfurl, and moist frass packed in the centre. The larva has a pale inverted Y on the head and four dark spots in a square near the tail.

**Stem borer** tunnels into the stem itself. You see small entry holes on the stem with dry frass at the opening, and in young plants the central shoot dies while the outer leaves stay green, which is called deadheart. Split a stem lengthwise and you find the tunnel.

The practical difference: fall armyworm can be reached by directing a spray into the whorl. A borer already inside the stem cannot be reached at all, so control there is about timing and destroying residues, not spraying.

Selling as a group opens buyers who will not deal in small quantities, and spreads the cost of transport, storage and testing across members. It also gives some negotiating position, which an individual smallholder arriving alone at a market does not have. The gain is usually larger than any agronomic change available in the same season. I want to start keeping rabbits. What should I know?

Rabbits suit very small capital: they breed quickly, eat forage rather than competing with the household for grain, and need little space. The failure point is housing. Hutches must stay dry and well ventilated but out of direct sun and rain, because rabbits tolerate cold far better than heat or damp.
What goes wrong when farmers do not apply fertiliser so it is not wasted?

Place fertiliser in a band beside the plant rather than broadcasting it across the field. Broadcast urea on hot dry ground loses a large share to the air before the plant ever takes it up, so you pay for nitrogen the crop never sees. Placement makes a small quantity work like a larger one, which matters most when cash is short.
What do I need to get right when planting soybean?

1. Rows about 50 to 75cm apart with plants close within the row, aiming for a dense even stand that shades out weeds.
2. Inoculating seed with rhizobium before planting is a small cost that raises nitrogen fixation and yield, especially on land that has not grown soybean before.

Walk me through planting yam on a small plot.

1. Seed yam of about 250 to 300g, or setts produced by the minisett technique, which multiplies planting material from a single tuber.
2. Large mounds or ridges for drainage and tuber expansion. Compacted soil produces short, forked tubers.
3. Staking lifts the vine into the light and raises yield materially over unstaked yam.

Check this against what your neighbours are seeing before you act on a whole field.

What goes wrong when farmers do not goat worms?

Worm burden rises in the wet season when larvae survive on pasture. Pale gums and poor condition despite adequate feed suggest a heavy burden. Rotate products rather than using the same one every time, because repeating one breeds resistance, and ask locally which still works.

Any advice on how to poultry water?

Birds go off feed long before they go off water, so a bird that stops drinking is in trouble. Clean drinkers daily, because warm dirty water grows the organisms that cause the scours you will be treating next week. In hot weather birds need far more water than feed by weight.

What is the right way to use mulch on my plots?

Mulch keeps soil moist between rains, holds soil temperature down and suppresses weeds, which on a vegetable plot can be worth more than an extra watering. It also protects the surface from the impact of heavy rain, which is what starts erosion. Crop residues, cut grass and leaves all work; the point is covering the ground.
How much water does rice need?

It depends entirely on which system you are growing in, and that is not me avoiding the question. The answer genuinely changes.

Which are you?

1. Upland rainfed, grown on ordinary sloping or flat land and depending on rain alone.
2. Lowland or fadama, in a low lying area that naturally holds water.
3. Fully irrigated with a controlled supply.

If you are lowland or irrigated, the practical guidance is to keep a shallow standing depth through tillering, and then drain the field before harvest so the ground firms up enough to work on. Continuous deep flooding is not better and wastes water.

If you are upland, you are managing rainfall rather than water depth, and your priorities move to weed control and choosing a variety suited to upland conditions. Tell me which one you are and I will be more specific.

Is fall armyworm the same as the armyworm that moves in swarms?

They are different pests with similar names, and the control differs.

**Fall armyworm** stays with the crop it hatched on. It feeds inside the maize whorl, is present in the field more or less continuously once established, and is the one that leaves frass in the funnel.

**African armyworm** moves in large migrating groups, strips foliage from cereals and pasture, and appears suddenly in outbreaks after certain rainfall patterns. It feeds openly on the leaves rather than hiding in the whorl.

If the damage is inside the funnel with frass, treat it as fall armyworm. If large numbers appeared overnight and are eating leaves in the open, report it, because outbreaks are managed at district level and your extension service will want to know.
What is the right way to coccidiosis signs?

Blood in the droppings, huddling, ruffled feathers and poor growth point at coccidiosis. Wet caked litter is the driver, so fixing litter and ventilation prevents recurrence better than repeated medication does. If what you see in the field does not match this, take a sample to an extension officer rather than guessing.

The rate is on the label of the product you bought. Your extension officer can confirm it.

I want to find out what my crop is worth. What should I know?

Prices move week to week and differ between markets, so a number quoted from anywhere other than your own market on the day is unreliable. Traders at the market, other farmers who sold recently, and farmer associations are the practical sources.
How do I get a better crop of groundnut?

Lift when the inside of the shell has darkened and veined and most kernels show their variety's skin colour. Left too long the pegs weaken and pods stay behind in the soil when you pull. Store in shell rather than shelled where you can, dry, off the floor and away from walls. Damp groundnut is the single largest aflatoxin risk in the food chain. Needs calcium available in the pegging zone for pods to fill. Poor filling on light soils often traces to this. Dry quickly and completely after lifting. Slow drying on damp ground is the main route to aflatoxin.
I tried that last season and the problem came back. Why?

Recurrence points at a carrier: infected planting material, crop residue left standing, or a neighbouring plot.
What is the right way to cope with rains that keep shifting?

Farmers across the region report rains starting later and stopping earlier than they used to. Shorter duration varieties and staggered planting hedge against a season that does not behave like the last one.
Is every problem on maize fall armyworm?

No, and assuming so wastes money.

Ragged holes with moist frass in the whorl is armyworm. Fine pale streaks along the leaf is maize streak virus. A purple flowered weed at the base with yellowing is striga. Small holes in the stem with dry frass and a dead central shoot is stem borer.

Match the symptom to the cause before buying anything. Each of those needs a different response, and three of the four are not helped by an insecticide.
I want to decide which fertiliser to buy. What should I know?

Buying fertiliser without testing is the most common way smallholders waste money. You pay for nutrients the soil already has while the one nutrient actually limiting your yield stays short, so the crop does not improve and the fertiliser gets blamed. A test costs far less than a season of the wrong input. Your extension officer will know where testing is available.
What will the rainfall be this season in Kano?

I do not know, and I have no forecast to give you. I also will not point you at a website, because I cannot verify one from here.

Your state agricultural development programme and the national meteorological agency publish seasonal outlooks. An extension officer will have the current one.

My maize has holes in the young leaves and there is something like wet sawdust in the centre of the plant. What is this?

Any advice on how to find out what my crop is worth?

Prices move week to week and differ between markets, so a number quoted from anywhere other than your own market on the day is unreliable. Traders at the market, other farmers who sold recently, and farmer associations are the practical sources.
